decision.quote: Our behavioral findings partially replicate previous results, showing that choice preference for alcohol was affected by the relative value of the alternative reward (Hogarth & Hardy,  2018 ; Karlsson et al.,  2024 ). In both groups, alcohol choice increased as alcohol was associated with more points compared to snack. Thus, alcohol was less favored when it was associated to the cost of losing the more valuable alternative reward, indicating similar sensitivity to cost in both groups.
decision.reason: The current new-sample scanner study explicitly compares its own relative-value alcohol-choice and AUDIT-choice findings with BOTH Hogarth/Hardy2018 and Karlsson2024, stating the prior AUDIT result came from two task versions and laboratories. This is direct retesting and own-result comparison, beyond mere task adaptation. The complete2018primary report identifies127Exeter student drinkers and the original alcohol-versus-chocolate relative-value/AUDIT findings. Current Methods power from that original and Results analyze the corresponding behavioral components. Existing988 represents the different Karlsson investigation; the current two-laboratory account positively distinguishes the prior reports, so the2018finding is genuinely absent. No crossed-delay outcome, original-cohort overlap or novel neural claim is inferred. Outcome is not requested. The final raw rationale contains unsupported original statistics: the actual2018relative-magnitude test is F(4,500)=20.79, AUDIT main effect F(1,125)=11.75/r=.29, and opportunity interaction F(4,500)=1.25,p=.289, rather than the final reply values. This independent source decision preserves that error and does not adopt it.

We hypothesized that patients with an acute episode of major depression are less able to intuitively discriminate semantic coherence from semantic incoherence in the JSCT than healthy controls.
decision.reason: Current H1 explicitly names both2015 and2017 as published intuition-deficit findings it seeks to replicate. The actual current test is semantic-coherence discrimination between diagnosed patients and controls, powered from2015; the2017abstract describes within-patient severity associations for semantic/visual intuition and a patient-control VISUALtask. These positive facts distinguish the exact comparisons but do not by themselves exclude a conceptual retest of the semantic depression/intuition claim jointly named in H1. Changing the contrast or task alone cannot establish background-only status under the codebook. Both original bodies and recruitment/report-overlap details remain unavailable after original-source attempts, so one cannot certify a separate closest-chain finding or report independence relative to represented2015row295. Retain this actual conceptual-finding/report-family allocation limit; do not assume extra unseen analyses, infer independence from DOI/year, or manufacture an additional pair. The two literal final expert exclusions and the earlier contrary positive remain preserved.
